visual.general_description: Two grayscale T2-weighted brain MRI views side by side: a coronal slice on the left and an axial slice on the right.
visual.detailed_description: Black-background grayscale MRI image with two views. Left: coronal slice through the brain at the level of the lateral ventricles, showing bright CSF in the ventricles and sulci, surrounding skull and scalp outline, and small printed orientation letters at the top and sides. Right: axial slice at the level of the deep gray nuclei and the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles, with small printed orientation letters (including "A" and "P") around it. On both views the deep gray matter region shows a symmetric pair of small, relatively brighter oval foci within darker surrounding tissue on the two sides. No arrows, panel letters, scale bars, measurements, patient text or other annotations are visible.

pixel_observations: Two views are shown side by side: coronal on the left, axial on the right.
Bright CSF signal in the lateral ventricles and sulci with darker brain parenchyma, as expected for a T2-weighted image.

A symmetric pair of small, relatively brighter oval foci is seen within darker deep gray matter on each side in both views; the image resolution does not allow a more specific anatomic or signal characterisation.
Small printed orientation letters surround each view; no arrows, panel letters, text overlays or scale bars are visible.
